messages.content: Write an announcement telling customers that a service is moving to a new platform next quarter. Around 250 words.

**Subject: [Service] moves to [New Platform] on [date]**

[Service] moves to [New Platform] in [quarter]. Here is what to expect.

Your account, your data and your billing history all transfer with it. Nothing to export, no settings to re-enter, no second sign-up. We run the migration ourselves, account by account.

Why now: the current system dates from [year] and the age is visible. Search times out on large accounts, the API stops at [N] requests per minute, and most of the features you have asked for need a rebuilt foundation first. [New Platform] gives us that foundation.

**What changes**

- The address becomes [new-url]. Old links redirect for 12 months.
- API keys stay valid. [old endpoint] retires on [date] and [new endpoint] takes over. Migration guide: [link].
- [Feature X] behaves differently, and the change is worth ten minutes of reading before your batch moves. Details at [link].

**What stays the same**: pricing, contract terms, and the people you email when something breaks.

**Timeline**: accounts move in batches beginning [date]. You get a notice two weeks before your batch, and another on the morning itself. Plan for about [N] minutes of read-only access during the cutover, scheduled for [time window] in your local time zone.

If that window does not work for your team, reply here and we will put you in a different batch.

Nothing else is asked of you before then. Send questions to [contact]. We are also running two live Q&A sessions on [dates] and posting the recordings afterward.

— [Name], [Title]

Two things to flag: I assumed a B2B or SaaS audience, and a migration we perform for the customer rather than one they perform themselves. If either assumption is wrong — self-serve consumers, or customers who have to act — then "what you need to do" becomes the lead and I would restructure around it. The bracketed items carry the weight here; without real dates and numbers in them, the announcement reads as filler.
Rewrite the text above. Keep the same length and the same purpose. Return only the rewritten text.

output:
**Subject: [Service] is moving to [New Platform] on [date]**

In [quarter], [Service] moves to [New Platform]. Here is what that means for you.

Your account comes with it, along with your data and every invoice you have ever received. There is nothing to export, no settings to key in again, no second sign-up. We do the migration ourselves, one account at a time.

Why now: the current system was built in [year], and it shows. Search times out on large accounts. The API caps at [N] requests a minute. Most of the features you have asked us for need a new foundation before they can exist, and [New Platform] is that foundation.

**What changes**

- The address becomes [new-url]. Old links keep working for 12 months.
- Your API keys still work. [old endpoint] shuts down on [date]; [new endpoint] replaces it. Guide here: [link].
- [Feature X] works differently now. Read [link] before your next batch run — ten minutes, and it will save you a support ticket.

**What does not change**: your price, your contract, and the person who answers when you write in.

**Timeline**: batches start moving [date]. You get two weeks' warning, then a reminder that morning. Expect roughly [N] minutes of read-only access during the switch, scheduled for [time window] in your time zone.

If that window is bad for your team, reply and we will move you to another batch.

Until then, there is nothing for you to do. Questions go to [contact]. We are hosting two live Q&As on [dates], recorded for anyone who cannot attend.

— [Name], [Title]
